source: Leatherworker world class, built against the shipped bestiary
note: Hides carry from_creatures: name fragments matched against bestiary names, so skinned loot can resolve to an entry here. Raw hides spoil (fresh_hours) until cured or tanned. Tier follows the CR of the beast the hide comes off: a deer is common work, a dragon is legendary work. Every entry carries `obtain` — harvested off a carcass, gathered where it grows, mined out of the ground, or bought with a price_gp — which is what the play page's acquisition hub offers as an excursion.

materials.name: Deer Hide
materials.text: Thin, close-grained and forgiving. It cuts quiet and stays soft through tanning, so a finished piece moves with the wearer instead of against them.

effects.target: Armour or clothing of deer hide never reduces the wearer's maximum Dexterity bonus

materials.name: Boar Hide
materials.text: Thick, bristled and dense enough to turn a glancing blade. It never fully softens: worked into armour it is proof but stubborn.

effects.target: ac
effects.note: against slashing weapons, worked into armour

effects.target: Stiff: the armour check penalty of a piece made from it is one worse

materials.name: Wolf Pelt
materials.text: A working winter coat. Cloaks and mitts of it keep a traveller moving through weather that stops lesser gear.

effects.target: survival

materials.name: Dog Hide
materials.text: Everyday leather, even-tempered on the rack. The first hide an apprentice ruins, and the second one they do not.

effects.target: Takes every method without complaint; apprentice work of it sells as journeyman work

materials.name: Cat Pelt
materials.text: Soft enough to line gloves and boot-tops; goods of it make no sound against each other.

effects.target: stealth
effects.note: lining boots or gloves — the leather is silent

materials.name: Horse Hide
materials.text: Broad, unblemished panels — the only common hide that comes off the beast big enough to cut barding from without a seam.

effects.target: Large single panels: barding and tents need no joining seams, which is where cheap barding fails

materials.name: Goat Hide
materials.text: Fine-pored and thirsty for the vat. Colours come out of goatskin true, where other leathers go muddy.

effects.target: Takes dye truer than any other common hide; dyed goods of it fetch half again the price

materials.name: Viper Skin
materials.text: Supple, patterned and near frictionless once oiled. Sheaths of it draw silent; sleeves of it slide out of a grip.

effects.target: escape artist

materials.name: Crocodile Hide
materials.text: Scaled ridge-plates down the back, soft belly leather beneath — two leathers off one carcass. The back turns a knife; the belly takes tooling.

effects.target: ac
The plate panels are stiff as green wood: check penalty one worse unless only belly leather is used

materials.name: Monitor Lizard Hide
materials.text: A cave-and-crag lizard's hide that keeps its suppleness through tanning where mammal hide stiffens. Armour of it bends where the wearer bends.

effects.target: Keeps its suppleness: armour of it never reduces maximum Dexterity bonus
acrobatics
effects.note: the leather flexes with the wearer

materials.name: Toad Hide
materials.text: Clammy in the hand and waterproof on the bench. Satchels of it carry powder and paper dry through a river crossing.

effects.target: Sheds water: contents of a toad-hide container stay dry through immersion

materials.name: Bat-Wing Leather
materials.text: Thin as good parchment and nearly as light. Too weak for armour, perfect for fine tooling, map cases and bellows.

effects.target: Takes the finest tooling; useless for armour — it tears like paper under a blade

materials.name: Weasel Pelt
materials.text: A trim fur, worth more as border than body. An edging of weasel marks a garment as bought, not bartered.

effects.target: Trim and edging: raises the finished value of the garment it borders

materials.name: Elk Hide
materials.text: Dense winter hide over large panels. Cloaks of it shrug off sleet, and the wearer's blood stays where it belongs.

effects.target: fort
effects.note: on checks against cold weather exposure

materials.name: Dire Boar Hide
materials.text: Everything boar hide is, doubled. Plates of gristle under the shoulder turn spear-points that would have gone through the beast's lesser cousin.

effects.target: ac
Heavy and stubborn: check penalty one worse

materials.name: Winter Wolf Pelt
materials.text: The frost never quite leaves the fur. A cloak of it is cold on the outside and warm within, whatever the weather is doing.

effects.target: cold
The fur stays frost-rimed in any weather; snow does not melt on it

materials.name: Boreal Wolf Pelt
materials.text: Longer-haired than the common wolf and oilier — weather runs off it. The pelt of choice for anyone who works outdoors in the white months.

effects.target: survival

materials.name: Black Bear Hide
materials.text: Deep-pile warmth. Bedrolls and sleeping furs of it turn a bare camp into a warm one.

effects.target: Sleeping gear of it counts as a warm camp in cold weather

materials.name: Grizzly Hide
materials.text: Worn as a mantle with the head and claws attached, it makes the wearer something other than a person to the people looking at them.

effects.target: intimidate
effects.note: worn as a mantle, head and claws attached

materials.name: Polar Bear Hide
materials.text: White cold-water fur over thick fat-backed leather. It hides a hunter on the ice and keeps the sea's chill out.

effects.target: cold
stealth

materials.name: Frostfallen Bison Hide
materials.text: A wall of a hide. One beast covers a warhorse in barding or a family in tent-leather, and the cold stays on the correct side of both.

effects.target: cold
Huge single panels: the largest seamless barding a tannery can produce below rare work

materials.name: Glowlizard Hide
materials.text: A faint mothlight lingers in the scales for a year after the skinning — enough to read by, too little to be seen by.

effects.target: Sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius for a year; enough to read by, not enough to reveal the carrier at distance

materials.name: Giant Frilled Lizard Hide
materials.text: The frill, worked into a collar, snaps open when the wearer squares up. People step back before they decide to.

effects.target: intimidate
effects.note: the frill worked into a flaring collar

materials.name: Electric Eel Skin
materials.text: Dry, it crackles faintly under the thumb. Gloves and grips of it spare the wearer the small revenges of wands, wires and storm-weather rigging.

effects.target: electricity

materials.name: Ankheg Shell Leather
materials.text: Chitin plates on a leather backing, the acid-etched channels still visible. It turns blades well and remembers the burrow poorly.

effects.target: ac
effects.note: plates worked over a leather backing

effects.target: acid
Plated and rigid: check penalty one worse

materials.name: Snow Leopard Pelt
materials.text: Smoke-grey rosettes that were built for exactly one job. In snow or broken shadow the wearer is a rumour.

effects.target: stealth

materials.name: Dire Wolverine Hide
materials.text: It stinks faintly forever, and it carries the animal's refusal in the grain. Wearers report a stubbornness that is probably their own.

effects.target: will

materials.name: Owlbear Hide
materials.text: Half plumage, half pelt, all argument. Cloaks of it shed rain like a roof and are impossible to mistake for anyone else's cloak.

effects.target: Sheds rain completely; the wearer and their pack stay dry in any downpour short of immersion

materials.name: Griffon Hide
materials.text: Feathered forequarters over lion-hide hindquarters. Falconers pay rare-work prices for common-work gloves of it.

effects.target: handle animal
effects.note: with birds of prey and flying mounts

materials.name: Shadow Mastiff Hide
materials.text: It drinks lamplight. Seams vanish in shadow, and so, very nearly, does the wearer.

effects.target: stealth
The leather is always slightly darker than its surroundings

materials.name: Salamander Hide
materials.text: Warm to the touch years after the beast died. Fire treats garments of it as a professional courtesy.

effects.target: fire

materials.name: Hell Hound Hide
materials.text: Char-black with a brimstone smell no tannin removes. It keeps fire off and puts the fear of somewhere else into onlookers.

effects.target: fire
intimidate

materials.name: Cave Bear Hide
materials.text: The biggest bear leather there is, thick enough that arrows read as rain. Armour of it is a wall the wearer carries.

effects.target: ac
Massive: check penalty one worse, and no piece of it is light

materials.name: Sabre-Tooth Tiger Hide
materials.text: The fangs, mounted at the collar, do the talking. The striped hide behind them confirms it was not bought.

effects.target: intimidate

materials.name: Basilisk Hide
materials.text: Stone-grained scale that takes a polish like marble. Heavy, handsome, and harder than leather has any right to be.

effects.target: ac
Polishes like marble; heavy — no piece of it counts as light armour

materials.name: Bulette Plate
materials.text: Landshark plates over boiled backing. Barding of it turns a lance, which is what it will be asked to do.

effects.target: ac
effects.note: overlapping plates, worked into armour or barding

effects.target: Rigid plate: check penalty two worse

materials.name: Manticore Hide
materials.text: Spike-pocked, every scar a socket. Tooled, the pocking patterns into relief work of unusual depth.

effects.target: The spike-scarred grain takes tooled relief work of unusual depth; masterwork tooling of it is famous

materials.name: Chimera Hide
materials.text: Three beasts in one hide — mane, scale and goat-shag — and no two panels match. A patchwork that arrives pre-assembled.

effects.target: fire
No two panels match: the dragon-third resists flame, the goat-third takes dye, the lion-third takes tooling

materials.name: Remorhaz Hide
materials.text: The beast ran a furnace under polar plating, and the hide keeps both opinions: it insulates against ice and shrugs at flame.

effects.target: fire
cold

materials.name: Gorgon Hide
materials.text: Iron-scaled and smelling faintly of rust. It takes metal polish rather than oil, and rings when struck.

effects.target: ac
Rings when struck; takes metal polish, refuses oil and dye

materials.name: Shadow Girallon Pelt
materials.text: Four-armed climber's fur out of the dark places. It grips stone and swallows light in the same motion.

effects.target: stealth
climb
effects.note: palm-panels grip like the beast did

materials.name: Nightmare Hide
materials.text: It smoulders. Whatever colour the vat held, the leather comes out black, and warm, and slightly ashamed of nothing.

effects.target: fire
Never takes dye: it comes out of any vat black. Faintly warm and smells of smoke

materials.name: Wyvern Hide
materials.text: Wing leather broad enough to cut a full cloak from a single panel, over body-scale dense enough for armour. The sting scars run through everything.

effects.target: ac
fort
effects.note: against poison — the venom's memory is in the grain

materials.name: Behir Hide
materials.text: Storm-blue scale off a beast that breathed lightning. Current refuses to cross it, which the beast never appreciated and the wearer will.

effects.target: electricity

materials.name: Purple Worm Plate
materials.text: Ring-segments the size of doors. Armour of it is tunnel-tested against rock, acid and everything the deep places threw at the worm first.

effects.target: ac
Enormously heavy: check penalty two worse

materials.name: Dragon Turtle Shell Leather
materials.text: Shell-margin leather from the beast that boils harbours. It keeps out steam, sea and swords with equal indifference.

effects.target: fire
ac

materials.name: Couatl Feather Hide
materials.text: Iridescent plumage over serpent leather, from a creature that was mostly made of goodness. Working it feels like being watched, kindly.

effects.target: will
Iridescent: shifts colour with the light and cannot be dyed, disguised or mistaken

materials.name: Hydra Hide
materials.text: Scar tissue that remembers regrowing. A rent piece knits itself closed over a week — the garment heals, though the wearer must manage on their own.

effects.target: Self-mending: damage to the finished piece closes itself over a week
swim
effects.note: sheds water like the marsh it came from

materials.name: Noble Salamander Hide
materials.text: What salamander hide wishes it was. It has opinions about fire, and fire has learned to respect them.

effects.target: fire

materials.name: Phoenix Feather Hide
materials.text: Feathers that ember at the edges without consuming. A cloak of it warms the dying and has, twice in the histories, refused to let them finish.

effects.target: fire
The feathers ember but never burn; the cloak sheds gentle warmth, and firelight through it casts no shadow

materials.name: Unicorn Hide
materials.text: Taking it is a crime the forest remembers. White past whiteness, warm as a living flank, and quietly good at keeping people alive.

effects.target: heal
effects.note: wound-dressings and sickbed furs of it

effects.target: The forest that lost the beast knows the wearer on sight

materials.name: Dragonne Hide
materials.text: Brass-maned lion-scale from the deep desert. The roar lives somewhere in it still: the mane bristles when the wearer raises their voice.

effects.target: intimidate
effects.note: the mane bristles when the wearer speaks

effects.target: fire

materials.name: Red Dragonhide
materials.text: Crimson scale off the tyrant of the colour chart. It smoulders in firelight as though remembering. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: fire
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it
Crimson scale off the tyrant of the colour chart

materials.name: Gold Dragonhide
materials.text: Metallic scale that was given, not taken — a gold parts with shed hide as a gift, and the leather knows the difference. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: fire
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it
Metallic scale that was given, not taken — a gold parts with shed hide as a gift, and the leather knows the difference

materials.name: Brass Dragonhide
materials.text: Talkative desert dragon's scale, warm as sun-struck metal at any hour. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: fire
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it
Talkative desert dragon's scale, warm as sun-struck metal at any hour

materials.name: White Dragonhide
materials.text: Scale the colour of old ice from the smallest and meanest of the chromatics. It frosts in warm rooms. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: cold
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it
Scale the colour of old ice from the smallest and meanest of the chromatics

materials.name: Silver Dragonhide
materials.text: Cloud-bright metallic scale. Snow slides from it; so, generally, does suspicion. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: cold
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it
Cloud-bright metallic scale

materials.name: Blue Dragonhide
materials.text: Desert-storm scale with sand still singing in the grain. Hair rises near it on dry days. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: electricity
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it
Desert-storm scale with sand still singing in the grain

materials.name: Bronze Dragonhide
materials.text: Sea-cliff metallic scale, green-shot like weathered statuary. It hums faintly before storms. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: electricity
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it
Sea-cliff metallic scale, green-shot like weathered statuary

materials.name: Black Dragonhide
materials.text: Swamp-black scale, glossy as tar. Acid beads on it and rolls away defeated. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: acid
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it
Swamp-black scale, glossy as tar

materials.name: Copper Dragonhide
materials.text: Trickster's scale, verdigris and bright metal by turns. It refuses to hold a straight seam and looks better for it. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: acid
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it
Trickster's scale, verdigris and bright metal by turns

materials.name: Green Dragonhide
materials.text: Forest-dragon scale smelling of chlorine and old leaves. Nothing rots it, and nothing eats through it. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: acid
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it
Forest-dragon scale smelling of chlorine and old leaves

materials.name: Umbral Dragonhide
materials.text: Scale from the dragons of the plane of shadow. Light near it gives up early; the grave's own chill runs off it. Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it.

effects.target: negative
stealth
Takes enchantment as masterwork armour; contains no metal, so a druid may wear it

materials.name: Tarrasque Plate
materials.text: A fragment of the armour of the thing that cannot be killed. Working it blunts tools; wearing it blunts everything else.

effects.target: ac
Nothing short of legend marks it: the finished piece never shows wear

materials.name: Kraken Hide
materials.text: Deep-water mantle leather, cold as the trench it ruled. It never dries out, never cracks, and remembers pressure no diver will meet.

effects.target: cold
swim
effects.note: the leather moves like water in water

effects.target: Immune to water damage and rot; the abyssal cold never leaves it

materials.name: Oak Bark
materials.text: The tannery's daily bread. Stripped in spring, stacked to dry, ground and steeped — brown liquor that binds hide into leather.

effects.target: The standard tanning agent for common and uncommon hides

materials.name: Sumac Leaf
materials.text: A pale tannin for pale work. Leather tanned with sumac stays cream-white and takes dye without a brown undertone.

effects.target: Tans white: the leather takes dye with no brown undertone

materials.name: Hemlock Bark
materials.text: Red-brown and fast. It tans in half the time and the leather comes out russet whatever was intended.

effects.target: Fast: halves tanning time; the leather always comes out russet

materials.name: Willow Bark
materials.text: A soft tannin for soft goods — gloves, linings, anything that touches skin all day.

effects.target: Tans supple: glove and lining leather of unusual softness

materials.name: Tara Pod
materials.text: Ground pods from dry-country trees, imported by the sack. Nearly colourless and strong — the choice for fine pale work above sumac's reach.

effects.target: Strong and colourless: fine work that must stay pale

materials.name: Bog Liquor
materials.text: Black fen-water, drawn where the peat has steeped for centuries. What went into a bog whole comes out leather; the vat merely hurries it.

effects.target: Tans deep black-brown through the full thickness; bog-tanned leather never rots

materials.name: Mangrove Bark
materials.text: Salt-swamp bark that tans against water. Boat leather, sea-boots, anything that will live wet.

effects.target: Salt-proof: the leather endures seawater without hardening or cracking

materials.name: Ironbark Tannin
materials.text: Bark off trees that turn axes. The liquor bites hides ordinary bark cannot touch, and the leather comes out with a metallic knock.

effects.target: Bites monster-grade hide that common bark cannot bind

materials.name: Wyrm Gall
materials.text: Rendered gall of the lesser drakes. Sharp enough to open scale that shrugs at bark liquor, foul enough that tanneries using it sit downwind of town.

effects.target: Opens and binds scaled hide; the stink takes a month to fade

materials.name: Salamander Ash Lye
materials.text: Lye of ash from an elemental fire, slaked with brine. It tans hides that fire itself could not mark.

effects.target: Binds fire-natured and planar hide; the vat must be stone — it eats wooden ones

materials.name: Styx Mordant
materials.text: River-water that forgets, cut a hundredfold and still dangerous. It fixes what nothing else fixes, and tanners who splash it lose the afternoon.

effects.target: Fixes shadow-natured and undying hide; a bare-skin splash costs the memory of the working day

materials.name: Dragonblood Tannin
materials.text: Tanning liquor quickened with the blood of the hide's own kind. Dragonhide accepts no lesser argument.

effects.target: The only tannin that binds legendary hide; the blood must be dragon's, though not the same dragon's

materials.name: Linen Thread
materials.text: Waxed flax cord, the tannery's default. Cheap, strong, replaceable.

materials.name: Sinew Thread
materials.text: Split leg sinew, chewed soft and dried taut. It shrinks as it dries and pulls every seam tight against weather.

effects.target: Shrinks tight: seams sewn with it are weatherproof

materials.name: Gut Cord
materials.text: Twisted gut, strong and slightly elastic. The stitch that gives before the leather tears.

effects.target: Elastic: the seam stretches under load instead of tearing the leather

materials.name: Horsehair Cord
materials.text: Braided tail-hair for decorative seams and edging. Not load-bearing; handsome.

materials.name: Waxed Heavy Flax
materials.text: Triple-laid flax dragged through beeswax. Saddlery thread — it outlives the saddle.

materials.name: Silk Thread
materials.text: Fine, strong and nearly invisible in a matched seam. Fine goods only; wasted on a satchel.

effects.target: Invisible seams on fine work; raises the finished value

materials.name: Spider Silk Cord
materials.text: Laid cord of giant-spider silk. Stronger than anything its weight has a right to be.

effects.target: Twice the strength of linen at a fifth the weight

materials.name: Wire-Silk
materials.text: Silk served around drawn silver wire — a smith's and a weaver's work meeting in one spool. Seams of it cannot be cut with a knife.

effects.target: Seams sewn with it cannot be cut by an ordinary blade; the wire is the blacksmith's work, not the tannery's

materials.name: Shadow-Silk
materials.text: Thread spun from the webs of the dark places. Seams sewn with it disappear in poor light, and so does the outline they define.

effects.target: stealth
effects.note: every seam of the piece sewn with it, in dim light

materials.name: Wyvern Sinew
materials.text: Wing-tendon sinew with a serpent's flex. The only thread that moves enough for hardened plate articulation.

effects.target: Articulation thread: hardened plate sewn with it flexes at the joints

materials.name: Dragon Sinew
materials.text: Tendon of the wing that carried a dragon. It does not break. The leather breaks, the needle breaks, the crafter's nerve breaks — the thread holds.

effects.target: Unbreakable: a seam of dragon sinew outlasts the piece it closes

materials.name: Neatsfoot Oil
materials.text: Rendered from cattle shin and foot. The everyday dressing that keeps leather leather instead of board.

materials.name: Currier's Tallow
materials.text: Hard fat for hard service. Boots and harness dubbed with tallow live wet and survive it.

effects.target: Waterproofs working leather against mud and rain

materials.name: Fish Oil
materials.text: Cheap, thin and pungent. The chamois-maker's oil — leather dressed with it comes out soft as cloth, smelling briefly of harbour.

effects.target: Softens leather to cloth-suppleness; the smell fades in a week

materials.name: Mink Oil
materials.text: Fine dressing for fine leather. It feeds the grain without darkening it, which cheaper oils cannot promise.

effects.target: Conditions without darkening: pale and dyed work keeps its colour

materials.name: Troll Fat
materials.text: Grease that remembers knitting flesh. Leather dressed with it closes its own scratches and scuffs overnight.

effects.target: Self-mending finish: surface damage to the piece closes overnight

materials.name: Salamander Oil
materials.text: Rendered from the fire-beast's fat, always a little above room heat. Dressed leather chars slower and never catches.

effects.target: fire

materials.name: Wyvern Fat
materials.text: Heavy amber grease rendered from beneath the wing. The traditional dressing for hardened plate: it soaks the boiled leather and keeps cuir bouilli from going brittle with age.

effects.target: Hardened leather dressed with it never grows brittle; the standard finish for masterwork cuir bouilli

materials.name: Umbral Oil
materials.text: Pressed shadow, or near enough. Leather dressed with it stops reflecting light entirely.

effects.target: stealth
The piece casts no highlights; in darkness it reads as a hole in the world

materials.name: Madder Red
materials.text: Root-red, the colour of soldiery and signage. Fast in sun and rain.

materials.name: Weld Yellow
materials.text: Clear bright yellow from a roadside weed. The cheapest colour there is, and the first to show dirt.

materials.name: Woad Blue
materials.text: Fermented leaf-blue, the working person's indigo. Deepens with each dip.

materials.name: Walnut Brown
materials.text: Hull-brown, needs no mordant, stains everything including the dyer.

materials.name: Iron Gall Black
materials.text: Oak gall and old iron. A lawyer's black — it does not fade, it does not forgive.

materials.name: Murex Purple
materials.text: Sea-snail purple at a thousand snails the ounce. Wearing it is a claim; be ready to defend the claim.

effects.target: The colour of rank: triples the finished value and gets the wearer noticed

materials.name: Vermilion
materials.text: Mineral scarlet, brighter than blood and twice the price of madder. Ceremonial work.

materials.name: Glowcap Green
materials.text: Fungal green that keeps a breath of the cave-light. Dyed work glimmers faintly in full dark.

effects.target: Glimmers faintly in total darkness — a finger of candle-glow, no more

materials.name: Shadow Black
materials.text: Blacker than iron gall by exactly the width of a shadow. Edges of the dyed piece are hard to fix by eye.

effects.target: stealth
effects.note: in darkness — the outline will not resolve

materials.name: Dragon's-Blood Crimson
materials.text: Resin-crimson, nothing to do with dragons, priced as though it were. It reads as embers in low light.

effects.target: Reads as live embers in low light; horses and dogs shy from the wearer

materials.name: Moonlight Silver
materials.text: Distilled from flowers that open once a month. The dyed piece is the colour of moonlight in any light, including none.

effects.target: The piece is moonlit in any light; in true darkness it sheds light enough to read a map by

materials.name: Void Dye
materials.text: Not a colour. An absence, bottled beyond the last plane and sold by people who will not say how. The dyed piece has no colour to name.

effects.target: stealth
effects.note: the eye slides off the dyed piece

effects.target: Viewers cannot afterwards describe the piece or its wearer's outline

materials.name: Thread Wax
materials.text: Thread-wax, edge-seal, and the smell of an honest workshop.

materials.name: Seam Pitch
materials.text: Seam-seal for wet service. Cheaper than beeswax, stickier, smells of forest fires.

effects.target: Seals seams fully waterproof; softens and smells in high summer

materials.name: Hardening Wax
materials.text: The cuir bouilli blend — beeswax cut with resins, ready for the kettle. Leather boiled in it sets like thin steel.

effects.target: The wax-hardening medium: boiled into leather it sets rigid without the brittleness of water-hardening

materials.name: Fireproof Wax
materials.text: Mineral wax that will not feed a flame. Finished work sealed in it chars grudgingly and never burns open.

effects.target: fire

materials.name: Ghost Wax
materials.text: Rendered from candles that burned in haunted houses, or so the seller says. Sealed work weighs less than it should.

effects.target: The sealed piece weighs half what it ought; contents of a sealed container do not smell, even to scent

materials.name: Iron Buckle
materials.text: The workaday buckle. Rusts if neglected, outlasts the strap if not.

materials.name: Brass Buckle
materials.text: Sea-service buckle: no rust, soft enough to bend before the leather tears.

materials.name: Steel Studs
materials.text: Dome studs for studded leather. The difference between leather armour and studded is a smith's afternoon.

effects.target: ac
effects.note: studding light armour — the studded-leather upgrade

materials.name: Bronze Rings
materials.text: Harness rings and strap-guides, cast by the gross.

materials.name: Silver Clasps
materials.text: Fine-work clasps for fine-work goods. Also the only fitting a lycanthrope's tailor will specify twice.

effects.target: Silver: the clasp counts as silver for what its touch harms

materials.name: Cold Iron Studs
materials.text: Studs of unworked-cold iron for buyers with fey trouble.

effects.target: Cold iron: the studding counts as cold iron for what its touch harms

materials.name: Mithral Fittings
materials.text: Buckles and plates at a feather's weight. The piece stops fighting the wearer's shoulders.

effects.target: Weightless fittings: the finished piece counts one step lighter to carry

materials.name: Adamantine Buckles
materials.text: Buckles that cannot be cut. A strap fitted with them fails at the leather or not at all.

effects.target: Cannot be cut or sundered; the strap fails at the leather or not at all

materials.name: Curing Salt
materials.text: Coarse salt by the barrel. Rubbed into a green hide it stops the clock that started at the skinning.

effects.target: Cures a raw hide: the spoilage clock stops

materials.name: Tawing Alum
materials.text: Tawing crystal. Alum-cured hide comes out white and soft but not properly tanned — it reverts if soaked.

effects.target: Taws white and soft; reverts to rawhide if soaked — not a true tan

materials.name: Brain Tan Paste
materials.text: Every beast carries enough brain to tan its own hide, an economy old as the first knife. Smoke finishes what the paste starts.

effects.target: The field tan: no vat needed, but the work doubles and the leather must be smoked

materials.name: Liming Quicklime
materials.text: For the liming pit: it burns the hair off a hide in a day. It will do the same to a hand.

effects.target: Strips hair and epidermis before tanning; caustic — handling it bare-handed is a burn

materials.name: Mordant Salts
materials.text: Fixing salts that marry dye to leather. Without them, rare colours walk off in the first rain.

effects.target: Fixes rare and exotic dyes permanently

materials.name: Planar Quench
materials.text: A sealed jar of elsewhere, opened over the hardening trough. Leather quenched in it sets with a memory of the plane it met.

effects.target: Hardened leather quenched in it keeps a planar trace: faint chill, faint heat, faint wrongness, dealer's choice
